findings.text: The first paragraph says plainly what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, so a newcomer can say what it is and why it matters within seconds.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: The second section on the page is an error message where the evidence should be. The lede promises to show models, cost and verdict, and the first proof shown is missing, which undermines trust.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The title and almost all of the content are about firstmate, a different project. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to work out that the page is a showcase and that the Athena content is only the lede and Next steps.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title> / "This page is that study of firstmate."

findings.text: What to do next is concrete: clone, install, then try a one-line request. Prerequisites are listed and the top of the page links straight to this section.
findings.source: Next steps: "git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The install steps do not say whether a paid model account or API key is needed or what a run costs. They also do not say what pressing Enter will do to the repository, such as making a commit, which a cautious newcomer would want to know before trying it.
findings.source: Next steps: "have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" / "press Enter to run it on your repository"

findings.text: This link in the header is aimed at the page owner, not a visitor. A newcomer meets it second, before any content, and it is unclear what it means for them.
findings.source: Owner view: "proposals waiting for your decision"

findings.text: The page is honest about gaps, but several terms used in the main flow are admitted to be undefined. The firstmate walkthrough is therefore hard for a stranger to follow, even though every claim is cited.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." / "The firstmate source does not define a durable record."

findings.text: The firstmate study is well organised for a reader who wants it: key words are defined before use, there is a step-by-step walkthrough, and there is a section on what goes wrong. Every statement links to file and line sources at the pinned commit, which shows Athena's tracing ability.
findings.source: Start here / One piece of work, start to finish

findings.text: The closing section refers to Athena's internal folder layout without a link, which means nothing to a first-time visitor.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
